items.name: GDS Holdings (China data-center operator; Q3 call Wed 25 Nov ~08:00 ET): 2026 CASH capex guidance cut to ~RMB 8.5bn from RMB 10bn (August guide) - CFO Newman on the call: the cut is a small change in the timing of payments to capex suppliers; capex INCURRED in 2026 still ~RMB 12bn (the gap is payables); organic capex RMB 4.3bn in 9M; asked directly by Morgan Stanley whether customers had delayed, Newman: payment timing only, no change to plans or execution; CEO Huang: delivery schedule will not change; bookings 686 MW in 9M toward a ~1 GW full-year target, >80% from the top three internet/cloud customers, domestic-technology orders only; backlog ~1.15 GW projected at year-end, billings 1.4 GW, RMB 16bn cost-to-complete over two years; utilisation 81.2% (79.2% Q2) 'highest ever', will 'dip back into the 70s' as new capacity comes into service (transitional); revenue RMB 3,180m +10.1% y/y
items.headline: GDS cuts 2026 cash capex guide to RMB 8.5bn from 10bn - management: supplier-payment timing, incurred capex ~RMB 12bn unchanged, no customer delays, delivery schedule unchanged; 686 MW booked YTD
items.candidate_dial: B2-capex (a principal 'capex cut' headline that does NOT fire the hard-event class on reading: the cash guide moves, the incurred guide and the delivery schedule do not, and the operator was asked the deferral question on the record and denied it - recorded so the orchestrator does not score the headline; it is also China-domestic-stack demand, outside the US hyperscaler chain; the 'utilisation dips into the 70s as capacity lands' line is the only digestion-flavoured sentence, and it is mechanical)
items.source: Motley Fool 'GDS (GDS) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript' (25 Nov 10:07 ET; machine-generated); marketintellabs 'GDS Q3: capex cut to RMB8.5B, data center utilization 81.2%' (25 Nov; AI-written, paywalled below the lede)
items.note: Transcript Q&A partly garbled per the fetch; the RMB 12bn incurred figure and the 'payment timing' explanation are management's, the 1.15 GW backlog is Newman's arithmetic on stated assumptions. GDS IR release not read. Stock reaction not printed.

items.name: Bank of America 'semis cuts have started' (Tue 24 Nov, relayed via CNBC's Quintanilla; Motley Fool 12:10 PST): BofA lists four cuts in eleven days, all on AI chips or memory - 13 Nov SemiAnalysis accelerator-capex forecast -28%; 19 Nov TrendForce Q1-2027 NAND contract-price outlook to flat-to-down 5%; 22 Nov Goldman 2028 SK hynix estimate -23% (Goldman 2028 price-decline forecasts widened to DRAM -19% from -5%, NAND -21% from -14%); 24 Nov BNP Micron downgrade (recorded 11-25). Counter-claims in the same piece: Micron said on its 30 Sep call that >75% of 2027 output is committed; contracted minimum revenue ~USD 134bn as of 3 Sep, ~USD 34bn due within 12 months (~an eighth of FY27 consensus revenue); Sandisk contracts cover >half of FY27 bits but ~20% of USD 88.9bn contracted revenue falls within a year; MU ~4x forward EPS at Monday's close, ~8x BNP's USD 86 trough; FY28 consensus EPS USD 206.65; Sandisk -12%, SK hynix -9% on the day; next test MU FQ1 17 Dec (guide midpoint USD 61.5bn, 86.25% non-GAAP GM)
items.headline: BofA: 'semis cuts have started' - four sell-side/forecaster cuts on AI chips and memory in 11 days (SemiAnalysis, TrendForce, Goldman, BNP); Micron's counter: >75% of 2027 output committed, USD 134bn contracted minimum revenue
items.candidate_dial: B2-capex / memory-no-surface (a framing item: the first house to label the sequence a 'cuts cycle' - still entirely forecaster/analyst-sourced, no principal, so not a hard event; the useful new data are the LTA-coverage figures (USD 34bn of the 134bn contracted within 12 months, i.e. ~one-eighth of expected FY27 revenue is contractually floored) which bound how much of the memory book an LTA renegotiation could touch - a query-5 reading the sweep had not found)
items.source: Motley Fool via Yahoo Finance 'Warning for Micron Investors: Bank of America Says Semis Cuts Have Started' (Chris Arnold; 24 Nov 2026 12:10 PST)
items.note: late:true - dated 24 Nov 20:10Z (inside the 11-25 window) but not in the 11-24/11-25 files; surfaced by sweep query 3 this run. The BofA note itself is not read (CNBC relay via an X post); the analyst is unnamed. The contracted-revenue figures are from Micron's own September disclosures as cited by the author.

items.name: Thu 26 Nov Asia - partial rebound and a BoK hike: KOSPI +1.2% to 4,755.29 (after -6.2%; Samsung +1.6%, SK hynix +3.7%; +1.7% at the morning snapshot), Nikkei +1.3% to 57,768.92 (after -2.8%; SoftBank +9%, Kioxia +12.4%, Tokyo Electron +1.5%), TAIEX +2.6% (TSMC +0.2%), Hang Seng +1.9% to 22,373.81, Shanghai -0.1% to 3,475.46 (holding its one-year low), ASX +0.9% to 8,767.20, Sensex +0.1%; USD/JPY 159.12, EUR 1.0961; Brent 91.11 (+0.5%), WTI 84.33; 10y UST ~4.86% little changed; JGB 10y 2.653% (from the 2.581% Wed low); Bank of Korea +25bp to 3.25%, 2026 growth forecast 3.9% (from 3.3%), 2027 4.1% (from 2.9%), Oct CPI 2.8% 'elevated for some time' on energy, exports +94% y/y in Oct to USD 115.3bn (chips ~half), 'robust AI investment' cited for the global outlook and the 'AI investment outlook' flagged as a market-conditions factor; AP drivers: S&P's Nvidia CreditWatch, 'calls for an AI slowdown on safety grounds', post-midterm buildout doubts, planned US tariff increases; US markets closed for Thanksgiving
items.headline: Thu Asia: KOSPI +1.2% (SK hynix +3.7%), Nikkei +1.3% (SoftBank +9%, Kioxia +12.4%), TAIEX +2.6% - about a fifth of Wednesday's loss recovered; BoK hikes to 3.25% and lifts 2026/27 growth to 3.9%/4.1% on chip exports
items.candidate_dial: C-equity (four-session Korea memory sequence now -3.3% / +6.3% / -6.2% / +1.2% - a dampening oscillation rather than a trend; the high-beta names (SoftBank, Kioxia) recovered most, the memory pair least, consistent with Wednesday's US pattern of 'everything but the capex beneficiaries') / business cycle (a second Asian central bank hiking INTO the AI export boom with growth forecasts raised ~0.6-1.2 pts - the BoK's own text treats AI investment as the upside and names its outlook as a risk factor, which the orchestrator may read against the US hot-data/hike-priced tape)
